title: "dicer token create"
description: "Make a token for the daemon's TCP listener"
---

Makes a token for the daemon's TCP listener, and prints it. It is shown
only this once: the daemon keeps only the SHA-256 of its secret.

`--scopes` says what the token allows: * for everything, which is the
default, or RESOURCE:ACTION, such as instances:write. RESOURCE is
instances, snapshots, networks, volumes, images, kernels, tokens or
events, and ACTION is read or write. Events have only read. A write scope
allows reading too. A token can make only tokens its own scopes allow.

`--secret-stdin` reads the token's secret instead of having the daemon make
one: at least 32 letters and digits. It is for a tool that must know the
token before it exists.

## Usage

```console
$ dicer token create NAME [flags]
```

## Examples

```console
$ dicer token create laptop
$ dicer token create ci --scopes instances:write,images:write
```

## Flags

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--format string` | Output format: table for the token alone, json or yaml. Default: `table`. |
| `--scopes strings` | What the token allows, comma-separated (default: * for everything). |
| `--secret-stdin` | Read the token's secret from standard input. |

## Global flags

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `-D`, `--debug` | Trace every call to the daemon on stderr (or set `$DICER_DEBUG`). |
| `-r`, `--remote string` | Daemon to talk to: a remote's name, or an address (unix:///PATH or HOST:PORT) (default `$DICER_REMOTE`, then the current remote, then local). |
| `--request-timeout duration` | Give up on a single call to the daemon after this long, e.g. 30s (0: never; streams such as logs -f and exec are not bounded). |
